conclusion.statement: Linear per-head readouts trained on training phrasings do not transfer relation atoms to held-out phrasings at splits 2 and 4. Whether the limit is the trunk, the readout, or template diversity (about 5 training templates per family vs 1-2 held out) is unresolved.
conclusion.separating_experiment: an MLP probe, other layers or positions, and an untrained-trunk baseline
conclusion.scope: not promoted; parked at this scope (D12: gates promote, they never kill): reading v2 entity/relation atoms and the semiprime joint key from the frozen S4 arm A trunk with linear heads at splits 2 and 4
conclusion.not_covered: joint training of trunk and heads; other trunks, splits, or read paths
conclusion.geometric_verdict: 2I parametrization neither promoted nor demoted (both arms under a failing guard)
conclusion.instrument_validation: not validated at the 2I arm: in-distribution guard fails for 2I (0.884/0.906) and narrowly for softmax (0.9799/0.9792) against >= 0.98
corrections: the earlier guard sentence conflated the in-distribution guard with held-out transfer; decode-1's guard-pass prediction was falsified

'the joint key is not recoverable' is contradicted by in-distribution key accuracy ~0.98; softmax split-4 key-correct 1517/3089 equals decode-1's relation-correct: the failure is held-out relation transfer

limitations: One frozen trunk, two splits, one world, one head family. A frozen-trunk probe decides only whether the atoms are readable there; it cannot show that a jointly trained model would fail. Held-out numbers are under the failing in-distribution guard unless stated otherwise. The executable-to-source binding is consistent but not independently verified (see executable.build_provenance).
